# How we rebuilt our room booking sheet

Hi, I'm Kenji from the facilities team. This post is about how we replaced the shared sheet we used for booking meeting rooms.

## A spreadsheet was not enough

Until last year, every booking lived in one spreadsheet. With 4 rooms, that worked fine. Anyone could overwrite anyone else's row, but with so few rooms and so few people booking them it rarely happened.

When we grew to 7 rooms this spring, the file became slow to open. Two people editing at once could wipe out each other's bookings. A meeting that ended early still held its slot. People walked to a room and found it empty more often than we liked.

## We added a panel at each door

So we put a small panel next to each meeting room door. We tested the panels on two floors first. Pressing the panel on the way out frees the rest of the slot. If nobody shows up within 10 minutes, the panel frees the slot on its own.

The panel and the booking screen read the same calendar. A booking made on one shows up on the other within seconds.

## What we learned

In the first week, almost everyone forgot to press the panel. We put a small sign on the inside of each door. By week 2 most people remembered.

The early morning slots still go unused. Old habits last. We plan to meet the office managers to talk about shorter stand-ups.

## What comes next

Next, we will add a chat message that tells people when a room frees up. We hope to ship it before December.

If your team would like to try the panels, come and find me on the 3rd floor.
